intro:
Khalkhin Gol

2 July 1939

Comrade Komkor, the Japanese have crossed the Khalkhin Gol. Tonight a force of the Kwantung Army is getting over the river near Bain-Tsagan, while its tanks press on our bridgehead on the eastern bank. They mean to cut the bridgehead off and take the crossings from behind.

Throw them back over the river. Three positions on this bank matter, and all three must be ours before the Japanese can dig in on them.

Your force is small but complete: rifles, the cavalry of our Mongolian comrades, armoured cars, tanks, guns and fighters. Choose carefully what you add to it now. You will be keeping it for a long time.

Do not underestimate the enemy. His infantry is well trained and does not surrender, and for the moment his pilots have the better of ours. What he lacks is weight: his tanks are light and few. Our own road is longer still - the nearest railhead is at Borzya, six hundred kilometres behind us - so what you have on the field is what you have.

briliant.text: The west bank is clear. Bain-Tsagan cost the Japanese the best part of a regiment, and what is left of their force is back across the Khalkhin Gol with nothing to show for it. In August we finished the matter: their 6th Army was encircled and broken, and on 16 September Moscow and Tokyo agreed a ceasefire on the frontier the Mongolians had always claimed. Your name was in the report.

victory.text: The Japanese are back across the river and the crossings are ours. In August the Army Group finished what you started, and on 16 September a ceasefire was signed on the frontier the Mongolians had claimed.

tactical.text: The Japanese are back across the river, but it took longer than it should have and our losses were heavy. The August offensive settled the matter, and a ceasefire followed on 16 September. Remember these first days. The next enemy will not give us so much time.

lose.text: The Japanese still hold this bank, and our bridgehead on the far side is gone. Moscow is sending another commander. Hand over your command and report to the People's Commissariat of Defence.

intro:
Suomussalmi

7 December 1939

Comrade Komkor, we have been at war with Finland for a week. Your corps is crossing the border in the northern forests with one task: take Suomussalmi and the villages around it, and open the road west to Oulu. If we reach the Gulf of Bothnia, Finland is cut in two at the waist.

Suomussalmi, Juntusranta and Piispajärvi must all be taken, and the road back to Raate must stay open behind you. It is the only road there is.

You will have little beyond your own troops. The rest of the army is on the Karelian Isthmus.

The reports say the Finns have few men here, almost all of them infantry. I believe the numbers. I do not believe it will be easy. The Finns are on skis, they know every trail, and the frost is already down to thirty degrees. Do not let your columns string out along the road.

briliant.text: Suomussalmi and the villages are ours, and the road is open behind us. The Finnish ski battalions that came for our columns found them in good order. The war itself was decided on the Isthmus, where the Mannerheim Line broke in February, and on 12 March 1940 Finland signed the peace in Moscow. It will not be the last war you fight. It may have been the last short one.

victory.text: Suomussalmi is ours and the road held. It was harder than the reports promised, as I said it would be. The Mannerheim Line broke in February, and on 12 March 1940 Finland signed the peace in Moscow.

tactical.text: We took Suomussalmi, but the Finns cut the road behind us more than once, and every kilometre was paid for. The peace signed in Moscow on 12 March 1940 gave us the ground. The whole army will have to learn the lessons of this winter.

lose.text: Two divisions went into those forests, and very little came back out. The Finns cut the road, surrounded the columns one by one and left the rest to the frost. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Minsk Pocket

26 June 1941

Comrade General, four days ago Germany attacked us along the whole frontier, and the Western Front is in a desperate position. Hoth's 3rd Panzer Group has passed Minsk to the north, Guderian's 2nd Panzer Group to the south, and they are reaching for each other behind the city. When they meet, everything west of that line is surrounded.

Hold Minsk, its airfield and the Berezina crossing at Borisov for as long as you can. If Minsk cannot be held, you have permission to take your troops out of it. Borisov must be held in any case, or nothing will get out at all.

You will have what the Western Front can give you: rifle divisions and a great deal of artillery, but very few tanks. The mechanized corps burned themselves out in the first three days.

In front of you is the bulk of Army Group Centre: tanks, motorized infantry, artillery, and bombers that own the sky. Watch for their 88 mm anti-aircraft guns, which they are firing at our tanks over open sights. Their men have two years of war behind them. Ours have four days.

briliant.text: Minsk held long enough. By the time the pincers closed, the divisions we needed were over the Berezina and moving into new positions. The pocket still cost us dearly, but the Germans did not get what they came for.

victory.text: We held almost everything we were told to hold, and a good part of the army came out through Borisov. It is not a victory. This summer, it is the next best thing.

tactical.text: It was very nearly a disaster. Minsk and Borisov held out longer than anyone expected, and that is the only reason there is anything of the Front left to rebuild.

lose.text: Minsk has fallen and the pocket has closed behind it, with hundreds of thousands of our men inside. There is no one to replace you and no time to look for someone. Take what came out with you and go south. The Germans are in Bessarabia too.

intro:
Defence of Kishinev

2 July 1941

The Romanians and the German 11th Army have crossed the Prut into Bessarabia. Their objective is Kishinev and the Dniester crossings behind it. Stop them. Hold Kishinev and the two positions that cover it.

You will fight with your own troops. The Southern Front has nothing to give you: every division it has is already in the line.

From the north comes the German 11th Army: experienced, well supplied, and the real danger. From the south-west the Romanian 3rd and 4th Armies are attacking. The Romanians are brave enough, but poorly equipped and new to this war. Your greener units will do better against them than against the Germans.

briliant.text: The Axis attack has broken on your lines. It has bought us the time to put Odessa into a state of defence, and the Romanians will not come on so confidently again.

victory.text: You held nearly all of your line. Kishinev will have to be given up in the end, but not today, and not cheaply.

tactical.text: Only one position held. Kishinev is lost and the front is falling back to the Dniester. We will have to do better at Odessa.

lose.text: Bessarabia is lost. The front is falling back on the Dniester in disorder, and the Romanians are marching on Odessa.

intro:
Battle of Odessa

28 August 1941

Odessa has been under siege for weeks, and in the last few days the Romanian 4th Army has pushed our lines back towards the city. Counterattack and throw them back: retake Razdelnaya, Vigoda and Yasski, and give the port room to breathe.

Your own troops will carry most of the weight, with what the Separate Coastal Army can spare.

The Romanian 4th Army is large but inexperienced, with plenty of cavalry and infantry and few tanks. Our intelligence expects German units to arrive within days to stiffen it.

briliant.text: The Romanians have been thrown back with a bloody nose, and they will not try that again for weeks. But Odessa is now an island. The Germans are on the Dnieper and the Crimea is threatened. The Black Sea Fleet will take your troops off by sea: the Stavka has a harder task for you at Kiev.

victory.text: The counterattack has thrown the Romanians back from the city. It cannot change the fact that the front has passed Odessa by. The fleet will take your troops off, and you are going to Kiev.

tactical.text: We have regained some ground, though not enough. Odessa will hold for a while yet without you: the fleet is taking your troops off and sending you north, to Kiev.

lose.text: The counterattack has failed and the Romanians are in the suburbs. Odessa will not hold for long now. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Kiev Pocket

12 September 1941

Comrade General, the situation is very grave. Guderian's panzer group is driving south behind Kiev, and Kleist's is driving north out of the Kremenchug bridgehead. If they meet, the whole South-Western Front will be inside the ring. The Stavka's order is to hold Kiev.

Hold the city and its approaches for as long as you can. Every day you hold is a day those German divisions are not on their way to Moscow.

Part of the 37th Army is under your command. The troops are raw and have few tanks, but there is some heavy artillery.

West of the city the German 6th Army is attacking with infantry and artillery. Expect their motorized spearheads to appear behind you from the north and the east: Panzer IIs and IIIs with lorried infantry, fast and dangerous.

briliant.text: You held Kiev and everything around it until the order to withdraw came. It came too late for the Front. But the men who came out of that ring came out through your sector, and the 6th Army will remember what the city cost it.

victory.text: You held most of the Kiev region to the end. The ring closed east of us all the same, and what came out of it is with you now.

tactical.text: Only part of the Kiev region held. The city fell sooner than it should have, and many men who might have got out did not.

lose.text: Kiev fell within days. The South-Western Front is gone, its commander is dead, and the road east is open. There is no time to find anyone else: you are needed at Bryansk.

intro:
The Bryansk Pocket

30 September 1941

Guderian has struck again. This morning his XXIV Motorized Corps broke through the Bryansk Front south of the city and is driving north-east. Orel is the obvious objective, and after Orel, our rear.

Give ground slowly and keep your army in one piece, but do not give up Bryansk, Orel, Dmitriev-Lgovsky or the Desna crossings before you must.

The 50th Army has been placed under you: some fifty units, most of them untried. Used well, they are enough to slow the Germans down.

The enemy has plenty of tanks, infantry and bombers. Expect heavy blows from the west and the south; his strongest group is in the south-west.

briliant.text: An outstanding defence. The German advance on this sector has stopped, and your army came out whole.

victory.text: You held most of the line. The army is battered but intact, and that is what Moscow needs now.

tactical.text: Most of the Bryansk region is in German hands. The army came out, but only just.

lose.text: The Bryansk region fell far too quickly, and the road to Tula is open. You will have one more chance, because there is no one else.

intro:
Counterblow at Tula

18 November 1941

The German drive on Moscow is faltering in the south. Guderian's 2nd Panzer Army has been beating at Tula for weeks, and it will attack your line south of the city again at any hour. Hold Tula, and as soon as the attack is spent, strike back and take their start line in the south.

You command the 49th and 50th Armies. The men are still green, but the divisions have just been brought up to strength, and a reconnaissance battalion has joined your command.

Parts of the 2nd Panzer Army are well below strength, and its first line is short of tanks and anti-tank guns. But Guderian still has panzer divisions in reserve, and he will commit them.

A great deal rides on this counterblow. If it goes deep, the Front has something far larger ready to follow it. If Tula only holds while the Germans slip past it, Moscow itself will need you.

briliant.text: This victory will be remembered for a long time. Your counterblow has torn open the German line south of Moscow, and we have taken back a great deal of ground. Now the Kalinin Front has broken through in the north as well. If the two blows meet, the whole of Army Group Centre is in the bag.

victory.text: Well done. We advanced along a broad front, but the Germans have brought up reinforcements and our offensive has run out of breath. There will be no further advance here this winter. Your army is going north-west, to Demyansk.

tactical.text: You won your battle, but the Germans may still win theirs. While you were fighting at Tula, their columns went round it, and now they are heading for Moscow. We need you in the capital.

lose.text: Tula is lost and the road north is open. German columns are heading for Moscow, and we need every soldier we have in the capital, you included.

intro:
Closing the Ring

17 February 1942

After Tula, the Kalinin Front broke through north of Moscow as well, and the two blows have met near Smolensk. Army Group Centre is surrounded. So far it has not tried to break out; I believe Hitler has forbidden it.

One gap is left. Your army will deploy north-east and south-east of the city and take the last two positions the Germans hold in the neck of the pocket. And whatever happens, hold both links to our troops in the east, or the ring will close around you instead.

We can give you little more than your own troops. Every other army is holding the ring.

The Germans in the neck of the pocket are weak, but they have mined and wired every approach, and they are not standing still. Divisions have been pulled out of Army Groups North and South to break in from outside, and the troops in the pocket will try to meet them halfway. Be quick.

briliant.text: The ring is closed. After a few days of hopeless fighting, the divisions in the pocket laid down their arms, and Army Group Centre no longer exists. Without it Germany cannot hold the East, and Berlin has asked for terms. The war is over. You have been made a Hero of the Soviet Union.

victory.text: The ring is closed, and the relief attack has broken against it. Army Group Centre has surrendered and the German government has asked for an armistice. The war is over, in 1942, against every forecast.

tactical.text: The ring held - only just, and at a terrible price. But it held. Army Group Centre has surrendered and Germany has asked for terms. The war is over.

lose.text: Our plan was too ambitious. The relief force has broken into the pocket, and Army Group Centre is getting out. At least your troops escaped the counter-encirclement. The Stavka has no reinforcements to give you: you go north-west, to Demyansk, with what you have.

intro:
Street Fighting in Moscow

5 December 1941

This is the last line. The Germans have reached the western outskirts of Moscow. Hold the city - every district of it - and when their attack is spent, throw them out of the suburbs.

You have a tank division, the Moscow garrison, and the bunkers and pillboxes built this autumn. We began mining the approaches, but there was no time to finish.

Expect several panzer and infantry divisions, and heavy attacks from the air. The Luftwaffe will be over the city every day the weather allows.

briliant.text: The German invaders have been smashed in the streets of Moscow. With their attack spent, our counterattacks have driven them back from the city along the whole front. Rest your men and wait for orders.

victory.text: Moscow has held. The Germans are falling back from the outskirts, and our counteroffensive is following them west.

tactical.text: Moscow has held, though whole districts are in ruins and the Germans have not gone back far. It is enough. The counteroffensive has begun.

lose.text: German troops are in the centre of Moscow. The government has left for Kuibyshev, and the war will go on from beyond the Volga - without you.

intro:
The Demyansk Pocket

20 March 1942

Comrade General, since the winter offensive we have held the German II Army Corps and part of the X in a pocket around Demyansk. They are being supplied by air, and now a relief group under General von Seydlitz is on its way to break in from the west.

Stop Seydlitz and keep the pocket shut. Hold the crossings on the Lovat, the Pola and the Rob'ya, and take the crossings on the Polomet' and the Yavon' from the troops inside.

You will have little besides your own army, and little room to deploy it. The ground around the ring is forest and swamp, and the thaw is coming.

The divisions in the pocket have been worn down by the winter. Seydlitz's group is about as strong, and much more dangerous; it will reach our western flank in about two days. Do not let it join up with the pocket. Several bomber groups have also been seen over the area.

briliant.text: The pocket has been destroyed before Seydlitz could reach it. Two German corps are gone from the map.

victory.text: The pocket has been destroyed. Seydlitz came close, but not close enough.

tactical.text: The pocket has been destroyed, but Seydlitz got within sight of it, and our losses were very heavy.

lose.text: Seydlitz has broken through, and the Demyansk garrison has its corridor. The whole winter's work on this front has been undone. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Defence of Voronezh

28 June 1942

The Germans spent the spring gathering their strength, and this morning they struck. Together with the Hungarians they have opened a great offensive, and its first objective is Voronezh. Slow them down so that we have time to prepare new positions behind you. Hold Zemlyansk, Nizhnedevitsk and the crossings on the Voronezh river.

You command the 40th and 13th Armies. With them are a few of the new self-propelled guns, straight from the factory. They could be useful to you.

You face the 4th Panzer Army and the 2nd Army, with the Hungarian 2nd Army supporting them in the south. The Hungarians are less experienced than the Germans. The Germans have new long-barrelled assault guns that outrange our tanks; watch out for them. And a report has just come in: more German troops, with good tanks and tank destroyers, are on their way. They will reach the southern part of the battlefield within a few days.

briliant.text: On this sector the great German offensive has been stopped before it truly began. Voronezh is ours, and it will stay ours.

victory.text: A sound defence. You held most of your positions, and Voronezh has held.

tactical.text: A clumsy defence. We had a good chance to stop the Germans well short of Voronezh, and you did not take it. The city has held, just.

lose.text: The Germans are on the Don at Voronezh. The line will be rebuilt behind you, and your army will be rebuilt with it.

intro:
The Rzhev Meat Grinder

30 July 1942

After the winter offensive the Germans still hold the salient at Rzhev, and it still points at Moscow. The Stavka has ordered it destroyed. Your army will attack at Rzhev in the north, at Sychevka in the south and through Zamyatino in the middle, break the line, and destroy or capture as much of the German force as it can.

You command the 30th Army. The Germans hold the only airfield in the area, but the army's engineers have plenty of experience building airfields in the field.

You face the German 9th Army, and the troops in the salient are still very strong. Their front is continuous and will be hard to break, but there is little behind it. The whole area is sown with mines and fortifications. Rzhev itself is heavily defended, and you will need long-range artillery to break in. Their reserves are at Sychevka, so expect hard fighting there as well.

Replacements will reach you every day of the battle. Use them: they cannot be saved for later.

briliant.text: The Germans have lost heavily, and the salient no longer threatens Moscow. And every division they sent to Rzhev is a division that is not going south to Stalingrad.

victory.text: Rzhev is ours and the salient is broken. The Germans had to feed into it divisions they badly needed in the south.

tactical.text: We have taken the salient's key points, but the price was appalling. The men already have a name for this battle, and it is not a kind one. Still, the German divisions held here are not at Stalingrad.

lose.text: The salient still stands, and we have nothing to show for our losses. In the south the Germans have reached the Volga. It will take a better general than you to stop them there.

intro:
Operation Uranus

19 November 1942

Today Operation Uranus begins: our great offensive to encircle the German 6th Army at Stalingrad. Your troops will strike the Axis lines from the north-west and from the south. Take Logovsky, Verkhne-Tsaritsynsky, Ivanovka and Vasilyevka.

The 65th Army is under your command. It will attack the Romanian front in the north and support your blow against the Italian and Hungarian troops in the south-east.

In the south-west, Hoth's 4th Panzer Army is your opponent. In the north the Romanian 3rd Army holds the line, and in the south-east there are Italian and Hungarian units. The Romanians, Italians and Hungarians are numerous but understrength, poorly equipped and short of ammunition. They should not stop you for long.

The 4th Panzer Army is another matter. It still has panzer divisions, and among them is a company of the new heavy Tiger tanks.

briliant.text: The ring around Stalingrad is closed. The 6th Army and part of the 4th Panzer Army are inside it, and the Axis armies outside have lost so heavily that a relief attack now has little hope.

victory.text: The ring around Stalingrad is closed. The 6th Army is trapped, and the Germans will have to scrape together a relief force from whatever they can find.

tactical.text: The ring is closed, but it is thin, and the Germans are already gathering a relief force. Hold on to what you have taken.

lose.text: The offensive the Stavka spent months preparing has failed. The 6th Army is not surrounded, and Stalingrad may not survive the winter. You are relieved of command and will answer for this in Moscow.

intro:
Battle on the Myshkova

12 December 1942

The Germans are trying to break into the Stalingrad pocket from the south-west. Hoth's relief group has reached the Myshkova river, and we have stopped it there. Now go over to the attack: overrun the enemy and drive him back to where he started, while Nizhne-Kumsky and Vasilyevka stay in our hands.

You will do it with your own tank army.

Army Group Hoth is on the far side of the Myshkova. We expect more troops to reach it over the next few days, but most of them will be Germany's allies rather than Germans.

briliant.text: Hoth's group is in full retreat, and the German front is now far from Stalingrad. The 6th Army is on its own, and it is doomed.

victory.text: The relief attack has been thrown back. The gap between the pocket and the German front grows wider every day, and the 6th Army will not be rescued.

tactical.text: Hoth has been pushed back - not far, but far enough. The 6th Army will not be rescued.

lose.text: Hoth has broken through to the pocket, and the 6th Army is getting out. Everything we won in November has been lost. You are relieved of command, and there will be an inquiry.

intro:
Kharkov: The Backhand Blow

15 February 1943

Comrade General, victory seems to be within reach - or perhaps it only seems so. The Germans are leaving the Kharkov area and falling back to the south-west. Your army is to push into the empty ground behind them and take Lyubotin and the roads beyond it, while Kharkov and Olshany stay firmly in our hands.

Many of our generals believe the Germans are beaten and the war will soon be over. I am not so sure. Be careful.

You will do this with your own tank army. Our reconnaissance reports almost no enemy in the area. I would not bet my life on our reconnaissance.

briliant.text: Your troops stood firm against the German pincers. Manstein's counterstroke has spent itself, Kharkov is still ours, and at last the initiative is ours too. I will insist on better reconnaissance before the next operation. Your men have earned a rest; we will call for you when the summer offensives are ready.

victory.text: Manstein's counterstroke has broken on your army, and Kharkov is still ours. The initiative has passed to us. Rest your men; we will call for you when the summer offensives are ready.

tactical.text: You held against the German pincers, though only just. Manstein's counterstroke has run out of strength, and the initiative is ours. Rest your men and make good your losses; the summer will need them.

lose.text: This defeat is not your fault. Our reconnaissance failed us badly. Your troops escaped the encirclement, but the Germans have retaken Kharkov. They will not stop there: they are gathering for a summer offensive against the Kursk salient.

dialogue.speaker: General Staff
dialogue.text: The Stavka does not want to move whole armies from one end of the front to the other for the coming offensives. Your army will stay on the sector where it is committed, to the end of the war. Choose where. — Army Group North: the shortest road. Lift the siege of Leningrad and follow the Germans into Courland. — Army Group Centre: the hardest. Smolensk, Belorussia, the Vistula and finally Berlin - or something worse, if our allies in the west play us false. — Army Group South: the longest. The Kuban bridgehead first, then the Ukraine, Romania and Hungary, all the way to Prague. — Two of these roads will not end in Europe. There is still Japan to settle.

choices.hint: Smolensk, Belorussia and the Vistula. The road ends in Berlin - or in a new war against the Western Allies.
The Kuban bridgehead, the Ukraine, Romania and Hungary. The road ends in Prague, and then in Manchuria.
Lift the siege of Leningrad, then Vyborg, Riga and Courland. The road ends in Courland, and then in Manchuria.

intro:
Prokhorovka

12 July 1943

The Germans are attacking our lines at Prokhorovka. Stop every attack, then counterattack towards Belgorod and take it.

We knew this offensive was coming and had months to prepare for it. Your tank army is not a veteran one, but every unit has been brought up over strength, and the ground in front of your start positions has been mined.

You face the II SS Panzer Corps. Expect heavy tank attacks, with the Luftwaffe close behind them; you will need strong air defence and fighters. Tigers, the first Panthers and new heavy tank destroyers have all been identified in front of you.

briliant.text: The Germans have been given a bloody nose. They have thrown in all their reserves and have nothing left for another great attack. North of the Kursk salient our armies have broken through the German lines, and the attack on the salient has been called off. And there is news from the west: the Americans and British have landed in Sicily.

victory.text: The German attack has been stopped and the salient holds. This summer the initiative is ours. And the Americans and British have landed in Sicily.

tactical.text: The line held, though our tank losses were frightful. The Germans have called off their offensive, and the Americans and British have landed in Sicily. The initiative is ours now.

lose.text: The German pincers have met behind Kursk, and several of our armies are trapped in the salient. The road to Moscow is open again. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Choice of Front

1943

The Stavka does not want to move whole armies from one end of the front to the other for the coming offensives. Your army will stay on the sector where it is committed, to the end of the war. Choose where.

Army Group North: the shortest road. Lift the siege of Leningrad and follow the Germans into Courland.

Army Group Centre: the hardest. Smolensk, Belorussia, the Vistula and finally Berlin - or something worse, if our allies in the west play us false.

Army Group South: the longest. The Kuban bridgehead first, then the Ukraine, Romania and Hungary, all the way to Prague.

Two of these roads will not end in Europe. There is still Japan to settle.

Leningrad

14 January 1944

For more than two years the Germans have held Leningrad under siege, and the city has starved. It is time to end it. In the south and the centre the Germans are already falling back. Hit their 18th Army hard enough and they will have to go here too.

You will have your own tank army, with two divisions of bridging engineers attached. The Germans have blown every bridge.

The 18th Army still has some good units, but the best German divisions are fighting in the south and the centre. Expect few tanks and a great deal of infantry.

briliant.text: The Germans have been driven back more than a hundred kilometres. On 27 January Leningrad fired its salute: the siege is over, and the city is no longer a hostage.

victory.text: The siege of Leningrad has been lifted and the Germans are retreating towards the Baltic states.

tactical.text: The siege has been broken, at a heavy cost, and the Germans got away in better order than I would like. But Leningrad is free.

lose.text: Leningrad is still under siege. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Vyborg

10 June 1944

The Western Allies landed in France four days ago, and the Germans are pulling troops west. Our next blow falls in Karelia. Advance across the Isthmus and take Viipuri - Vyborg, as it will be called again. Terijoki, Rautu, Taipale and Heinjoki lie on the way.

You will have only your own tank army.

You face the Finnish army, which will defend every line on the Isthmus, and you should expect the Germans to send it some help. Even so, the enemy should not be able to stop you.

briliant.text: Vyborg fell on schedule and the Finnish front on the Isthmus has collapsed. Finland has asked for an armistice, and under its terms the Finnish army will turn against the Germans in Lapland.

victory.text: Vyborg is ours. Finland has asked for an armistice, and its army will now turn against the Germans.

tactical.text: Vyborg is ours, though the Finns made us pay for every line. Finland has asked for an armistice.

lose.text: The Finns have held the Isthmus. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Riga

14 September 1944

After Karelia, the Baltic. Your tank army is to attack the Germans at Riga and drive them out of the city.

You will have only your own tank army.

The German 16th and 18th Armies are defending. There are strong panzer divisions outside the city, and in Riga itself fanatical infantry, with plenty of artillery behind it.

After Riga your army goes straight on into Courland, and from there far to the east. There will be no quiet refit between those battles, so do not burn out your units here.

briliant.text: Riga is free. The Germans have fallen back into Courland, and they are trapped there.

victory.text: Riga is free, and the Germans have fallen back into Courland.

tactical.text: Riga is free, but it was costly. The Germans have fallen back into Courland.

lose.text: The attack on Riga failed at the first line. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Courland Pocket

12 February 1945

We have tried several times to destroy the Germans trapped in Courland, and every attempt has failed. I think your men are the right ones for the job. Attack on the front between Liepaja and Saldus, break through and take Pavilosta on the coast. Liepaja and its airfield, Skrunda and Saldus must fall too.

You will have only your own tank army.

You face the 16th and 18th Armies. They are worn down but very experienced, and they still have two strong panzer units. The approaches are blocked with obstacles, bunkers and minefields.

briliant.text: The Courland pocket has been destroyed, and the troops it tied down can go to Berlin. The end of the war is near - but not for you. We have agreed with the Western Allies to attack Japan in the summer, and your army is going east.

victory.text: Courland has fallen. The war in Europe is almost over, but your army has a longer road ahead: we have promised the Allies to attack Japan in the summer.

tactical.text: Courland has fallen at last, and at a heavy price. Rest your men on the way east. We have promised the Allies to attack Japan in the summer.

lose.text: Yet another attack on Courland has failed. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Manchurian Operation

9 August 1945

The war in Europe is over. Now we keep our promise to the Allies and open a second front against Japan. Your army is to break through the Japanese and Manchukuo lines east of Changchun, then take Changchun, Jilin and Siping.

You will have only your own tank army. We hold no airfield in this area, so bring engineers who can build one.

You face two Japanese armies and Manchukuo troops. They are poorly equipped, but they have dug themselves into the mountains east of Changchun, and breaking through will take time.

briliant.text: After the Germans, the Japanese. The Kwantung Army has surrendered, and Japan is out of the war. It is over - truly over. You and your men have earned every honour that is coming to you. Come home to Moscow.

victory.text: The Kwantung Army has surrendered, and Japan is out of the war. It is over. Come home to Moscow.

tactical.text: The Kwantung Army has surrendered. The mountains cost us more than they should have, but the war is over. Come home.

lose.text: The attack stalled in the mountains. It makes no difference to the outcome - Japan has surrendered all the same - but it makes a difference to you. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Smolensk Offensive

7 August 1943

Now our great offensive begins. You will attack Army Group Centre at Yelnya. The Germans have had time to prepare, but I am sure you can break through. Take Yelnya, Glinka and the villages along the German line.

You will have only your own tank army.

Army Group Centre is still strong, though short of tanks. Expect heavy long-range artillery fire, and the Luftwaffe has a strong bomber force here. The ground behind the river crossings is well fortified, but once you are through, resistance will be lighter.

briliant.text: We have taken back a great deal of ground and destroyed several German divisions. Smolensk will be free within weeks. The Stavka is planning new offensives, and we will tell you when your troops are needed.

victory.text: The German line at Yelnya has been broken, and Smolensk will soon be free. Rest your men; new offensives are coming.

tactical.text: We broke through at Yelnya, though the German artillery made us pay for every crossing. Smolensk will soon be free.

lose.text: Our first great offensive in the centre has failed. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Operation Bagration

22 June 1944

The time has come for our greatest offensive. Several fronts are joining the attack in Belorussia. Your task is Vitebsk: take the city and push on to the west, to Gorodok, Polotsk and Lepel.

You will have only your own tank army.

Vitebsk is protected by strong fortifications and held by the LIII Army Corps; further south, the VI Army Corps holds the line. The Germans have good tanks and tank destroyers here, among them Tiger IIs and a unit of Ferdinands. It might be wise to put your best troops in the south, break through there, and let the rest close in on Vitebsk.

briliant.text: The offensive has been a great success. We have not only freed Belorussia but reached the Vistula. Comrade Stalin has decorated you.

victory.text: Belorussia is free, and our armies are on the Vistula.

tactical.text: Belorussia is free and our armies are on the Vistula, but your sector cost more than any other.

lose.text: Our great offensive stuck at the first German line, and many men died for nothing. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Kraków

17 January 1945

Our armies are crossing Poland. Your task is Kraków, to the west of you: take the city, its two airfields and the towns around it.

You will have only your own tank army.

Kraków is held by the German 17th Army, with what is left of the 4th Panzer Army. They are far under strength, but they still have some formidable Panthers and Tiger IIs. The hardest fighting will be in the city itself.

After Kraków you go straight on to the Oder, and then to Berlin, with no time to refit between the battles. Bring your units out of this one in good order.

briliant.text: Kraków has been taken almost intact, before the Germans could destroy it or pull their troops out.

victory.text: Kraków is free. The Germans are falling back to Silesia and the Oder.

tactical.text: Kraków is free, though the fighting in the streets was hard. The road to the Oder is open.

lose.text: The attack on Kraków has failed. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Fortress Küstrin

26 March 1945

Your troops have reached the Oder at Küstrin. Take the fortress and the villages around it, secure the river line, and build a bridgehead on the far bank.

You will have only your own tank army.

Küstrin is held by its garrison, and beyond the Oder strong German forces will try to stop your bridgehead. Taken together, they should not be a problem for your troops.

Speed matters more than usual here. Our allies in the west are also racing for Berlin, and the agreements about who takes the city are only as strong as our position on the Oder.

briliant.text: The road to Berlin is open. As soon as our operations in the north are finished, your troops will attack.

victory.text: The Western Allies have broken our agreements and taken Berlin. This will not go unanswered: we are at war with them. There is one advantage. The German armies in the east have surrendered to us, and their commanders have agreed to fight beside us in return for their men being spared the camps. German units are available to you if you need them.

tactical.text: The Western Allies have broken our agreements and taken Berlin, and we are at war with them. Worse, the German armies in the east have slipped away to the west, and they will fight alongside the Allies against us.

lose.text: The Oder crossing has failed. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Battle of Berlin

16 April 1945

Comrade General, this is the last battle. Your troops are in position on the Oder, and there is a great deal to do:
- cross the Oder at the Seelow Heights and destroy the 9th Army;
- take Frankfurt, Cottbus, Schwedt and Oranienburg;
- surround what is left of the 9th Army near Halbe, and let none of it break out to the west;
- take Berlin and Potsdam;
- stop Wenck's 12th Army coming from the Elbe, and take Wittenberg.

The 2nd Belorussian Front will support you in the north, where it will take Schwedt and deal with the 3rd Panzer Army, and the 1st Ukrainian Front will support you in the south. This is the last battle, so spend everything you have: replacements are waiting for you.

The 9th Army, the 12th Army and the 4th Panzer Army are veteran but worn out. They still have Tiger IIs and Panthers, and our intelligence even speaks of super-heavy prototypes. Around Berlin you will also meet the Volkssturm and the Hitler Youth. The city itself is defended by the remnants of the 9th Army, police units, the Volkssturm and SS Battle Group Mohnke.

briliant.text: Berlin has fallen. Hitler is dead, and the German surrender is a matter of days. It is over. Come home: Moscow is waiting to celebrate with you.

victory.text: The Red Banner is flying over the Reichstag. Germany is finished. Come home.

tactical.text: Berlin is ours, though the Halbe pocket cost us more than it should have. The war in Europe is over. Come home.

lose.text: So close. The Halbe pocket leaked, the German armies got away to the west, and Berlin has not fallen to us. Others will have to finish what you started.

intro:
Breakthrough at Dessau

19 May 1945

After careful planning, the General Staff has decided to strike the Allied lines at Dessau. The Allies have concentrated a great many troops on this sector; if we break through here, they will have to pull back everywhere else. Take Dessau, Halle and Merseburg, and push on to Stassfurt and Quedlinburg.

Besides your tank army, a second army will support the attack from positions west of yours.

The enemy has several armoured divisions. German units that went over to the Allies in the spring are fighting in their ranks. Expect strong opposition in the air: the USAAF and the RAF have several air forces around Dessau, and heavy bombers will support their ground troops.

briliant.text: Your troops have broken through the Allied lines, and their losses have forced them to fall back all along the front.

victory.text: The Allied line at Dessau is broken, and they are falling back.

tactical.text: We broke through at Dessau, but their aircraft made us pay for every kilometre.

lose.text: The offensive has failed, and the war is over on their terms. We will have to live with the betrayal of our western allies.

intro:
Battle of East Frisia

23 June 1945

We have trapped several Allied armies in East Frisia. We know they plan to evacuate them by sea through Emden and Wilhelmshaven. Take both ports before the ships arrive, and destroy as much of the trapped force as you can, so that it never comes back at us.

Besides your tank army, a smaller army will support you; its troops will be useful for the attack on Emden.

The trapped enemy still has dangerous armoured divisions and plenty of infantry. German units that went over to the Allies in the spring are fighting in their ranks. Their air force will give you trouble, all the more because you have no airfield at the start and the nearest one is too far away. Make sure you have engineers who can build one.

briliant.text: The trapped Allied armies have been destroyed, and with Emden and Wilhelmshaven the Allies have lost two ports where they could land new troops.

victory.text: Emden and Wilhelmshaven are ours, and most of the trapped force will never fight again.

tactical.text: Emden and Wilhelmshaven are ours, though too many of the trapped troops got onto the ships.

lose.text: The Allied troops have got away by sea. The war will last longer than we hoped - but not for you. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Battle of the Ruhr

26 July 1945

The factories of the Ruhr are working for the Western Allies now. Take the Ruhr from them and their armies on the continent will be much harder to supply. Take the Ruhr cities and Düsseldorf, and build a bridgehead over the Rhine.

Besides your tank army, several divisions will support you. At your request we have given you more anti-aircraft units.

The enemy is not numerous. East of the Ruhr the Allies have built a line protected by obstacles, minefields and barbed wire; further south the resistance seems lighter.

briliant.text: The Ruhr is ours. After this we can take the whole of Germany within months. The German units in Allied service are surrendering to us by whole battalions.

victory.text: The Ruhr and Düsseldorf are ours, and we are over the Rhine. The German units in Allied service are surrendering to us by whole battalions.

tactical.text: The Ruhr is ours, but the bridgehead over the Rhine is a narrow one. The German units in Allied service are surrendering to us by whole battalions.

lose.text: You were not fast enough, and the Ruhr is still theirs. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Ardennes

20 August 1945

Where the Germans failed, we intend to succeed. In the Ardennes the Allies have built their last defensive line. If we break through, the road to Antwerp is open, and the Allies can no longer use its port to bring in reinforcements.

Another army will support your attack, and a unit of IS heavy tanks has been attached to you.

The Allies are still numerous. Beware of ambushes in the woods, and remember that the IS tanks carry very little ammunition and are vulnerable in this terrain.

briliant.text: The last serious Allied force has been beaten, and the road to Antwerp is open. A fine piece of work.

victory.text: The Allied line in the Ardennes has broken, and the road to Antwerp is open.

tactical.text: We are through the Ardennes, though the forest cost us dearly. The road to Antwerp is open.

lose.text: Our offensive has broken down just as the German one did. Before the Allies can push us back to the German border, the Stavka is appointing a new commander.

intro:
Assault on Antwerp

10 October 1945

Victory is close. Your troops are on the approaches to Antwerp. Destroy the last Allied troops and take the port, so that no more Allied reinforcements can land.

Several ships cover the harbour, so part of our fleet has been placed under your command, and bombers will support you. The Allies hold the only airfield in the area; it would be wise to build one of your own at the start of the battle.

The Allies have abandoned the ground south of the city and covered it with mines and obstacles. Beyond that line their front is thin. Further back they still have heavy tanks - Shermans of the latest type - and green armoured divisions are unloading in the harbour right now.

briliant.text: Antwerp is ours, taken in barely half a year of war. The Allies have no port left close enough to land a new army, and they have understood it: they have asked for peace. The whole of Germany is in our hands. You are invited to the Kremlin, where Comrade Stalin wishes to thank you in person.

victory.text: Antwerp is ours. With no port left to land a new army, the Allies have asked for peace, and the war is over. Moscow is waiting for you.

tactical.text: Antwerp is ours, though the harbour fighting was brutal. The Allies have asked for peace, and the war is over.

lose.text: The assault on Antwerp has been a disaster. The Allies have heavily reinforced the harbour, and a new offensive is impossible for now. Your troops will be rested - under a new commander.

intro:
The Kuban Bridgehead

3 September 1943

For months the Germans have held their bridgehead on the Black Sea coast. We have pushed them back, but every attempt to destroy them has failed. Now we know they intend to evacuate it before they are cut off, and we will attack before they can get away. Break the line, take Novorossiysk, Krymsk, Anapa and Taman, and destroy the German forces.

You will have only your own tank army. The Germans hold both airfields in the area, but an engineer unit has been attached to you, and it should be able to build a small airfield within a few days.

You face the German 17th Army, with Romanian and Slovak troops. The Romanians and Slovaks are weak. The Germans have few tanks and only one fighter group. There may be no great counterattack, but you must be quick.

briliant.text: The Axis forces have lost heavily, and nothing got away across the Kerch Strait. Meanwhile we have pushed forward in the Ukraine. Your men need a rest, and I am sure they will be needed again soon.

victory.text: The Kuban bridgehead is gone, and most of the 17th Army with it. Rest your men.

tactical.text: The Kuban bridgehead is gone, though a good part of the 17th Army got across to the Crimea. Rest your men.

lose.text: Much of the Axis force got away across the Kerch Strait because of your failure. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Counterattack at Zhitomir

13 November 1943

I am sorry to cut your rest short. While your troops were refitting, the situation near Zhitomir has turned serious. After we retook Kiev, the Germans counterattacked with several panzer divisions. Hold Zhitomir and Korostyshev, and stop any advance on Kiev.

Because of the refit, not all of your units could set out together. At first you will have only a few troops near Zhitomir; the rest will come up over the next days. The 94th Rifle Division is defending Zhitomir, and it is under your command.

The Germans are not numerous, but some of their tanks are formidable, and they are very close to Zhitomir. A sudden blow could be devastating. Be careful.

briliant.text: The German counterattack has been stopped dead, and it has cost them a great many men and tanks. I doubt they can mount another.

victory.text: The German counterattack has been stopped, and Kiev is safe.

tactical.text: The German counterattack has been stopped, but only just short of Kiev.

lose.text: The Germans have destroyed several of our divisions and are at the gates of Kiev. We can only hope that reinforcements arrive in time. You are relieved of command.

intro:
The Brody Cauldron

20 July 1944

With your advance, the ring around the German divisions at Brody is closed. They will try to break out. Stop them from getting across the river to the west, destroy as much of the encircled force as you can, and keep Lutsk in our hands.

Troops of the 1st Ukrainian Front will support you.

You face the XIII Army Corps. It is under strength and has only a few serious tanks. With a solid front, the breakout should not be hard to stop.

briliant.text: The Brody pocket has been destroyed, and the road to Lwów is open. Next comes Romania.

victory.text: The Brody pocket has been destroyed. Next comes Romania.

tactical.text: The Brody pocket has been destroyed, though more of them got out than I would have liked. Next comes Romania.

lose.text: Too many of them got out. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Jassy-Kishinev

20 August 1944

Romania must be knocked out of the war. Without the Romanian oilfields, the Germans cannot keep up serious resistance for long. Break through the Axis line at Jassy and push on to Piatra Neamț.

You will have only your own tank army.

You face Army Group South Ukraine: Army Group Wöhler and Army Group Dumitrescu, each a mixture of German and Romanian armies. The Germans have some heavy tanks and will counterattack hard if your first blow is weak. The Romanians have lost heavily in this war, and their units are well below strength.

briliant.text: Romania has changed sides. On 23 August the King had Antonescu arrested and asked for an armistice, and the Germans have lost the oilfields at Ploesti. Without fuel their army will soon stop moving. The end is in sight.

victory.text: Romania has left the war, and the Germans have lost the oilfields at Ploesti. The road to Hungary is open.

tactical.text: Romania has left the war, though the German counterattacks cost us dearly. The road to Hungary is open.

lose.text: Our offensive does not deserve the name. Romania is still fighting alongside the Germans. You are relieved of command.

intro:
Székesfehérvár

16 March 1945

While the Germans try to break through our lines at Lake Balaton, your task is to break through the German and Hungarian line at Székesfehérvár. Take the city, its airfield and Nádasladány. With the city in our hands, the road to Vienna is open.

You will have only your own tank army.

You face Army Group Balck. Its troops are exhausted, but they still have some strong tanks and fighters.

After this battle your army goes straight on into Czechoslovakia, and from there far to the east. There will be no quiet refit in between, so bring your units out of this one in good order.

briliant.text: The road to Vienna is open, and the Germans have had to call off their offensive at Lake Balaton.

victory.text: Székesfehérvár is ours, and the German offensive at Lake Balaton has been called off.

tactical.text: Székesfehérvár is ours, though the German tanks made it a hard fight.

lose.text: No breakthrough, no further command. It is that simple.

intro:
The Road to Prague

6 May 1945

Berlin has fallen. Now we must destroy the German armies still fighting in Czechoslovakia and free Prague. Your road north begins on the Hron: break the German line at Nagysalló, take Léva and Lök, and advance north.

The 2nd Ukrainian Front will support your attack, and Romanian, Czechoslovak and Polish troops are under your command. There is no airfield in the area, so you will have to build one before your aircraft can fly.

You face the German 8th Army. It has lost much of its strength, but in the last few days it has received some experimental heavy tanks, straight from the proving grounds. The Germans also have new fighters here, but no airfield nearby, so they can support their troops for only a few days.

briliant.text: You have broken the German line and destroyed the 8th Army. The road to Prague is open, and the war in Europe is over. But not for your army: it is going east, against Japan.

victory.text: The German line has broken and the road to Prague is open. The war in Europe is over, and your army is going east, against Japan.

tactical.text: We are through, though the 8th Army fought to the last. The war in Europe is over, and your army is going east, against Japan.

lose.text: You have failed. You are relieved of command.
